title: Check: Gateway API
description: Five questions on the successor to Ingress.

questions.prompt: What problem does the Gateway API set out to solve?

options.text: Ingress packs every feature into annotations and mixes operator and developer concerns

questions.explanation: Gateway API splits the roles into separate resources with a real schema instead of vendor-specific annotations.

questions.prompt: Which are Gateway API resources? Choose all that apply.
questions.explanation: GatewayClass is the infrastructure type, Gateway an instance, HTTPRoute the routing rules. IngressClass belongs to the older API.

questions.prompt: Who typically owns the Gateway, and who owns the HTTPRoute?

options.text: The cluster operator owns the Gateway; application teams own HTTPRoutes

questions.explanation: That separation is the whole point: infrastructure is configured once, routes are attached to it by the teams that own the apps.

questions.prompt: How does the Gateway API ship?

options.text: As CRDs you install into the cluster
As part of the CNI plugin

questions.explanation: The CRDs plus a controller that implements them. Nothing is built in yet.

questions.prompt: What lets an HTTPRoute in one namespace attach to a Gateway in another?

options.text: The Gateway's allowedRoutes, and a ReferenceGrant for cross-namespace backends

questions.explanation: Explicit permission in both directions is deliberate - it is what stops a team from hijacking someone else's hostname.
